components.note: 着 developed as a graphic variant of 著 (zhù), which combined 艹 (grass) over 者 (a person); the original sense was 'to attach, to wear,' later extended to 'to touch down, to arrive,' as in 着陆 'to land.'
阝 (a hill/place) — 陆 relates to solid ground, as opposed to water
击 (jī) gives a sound distantly related to 陆's reading lù, having drifted apart considerably over time

example.hanzi: 那架飞机安全着陆了。
example.pinyin: Nà jià fēijī ānquán zhuólù le.
example.english: That airplane landed safely.
example.fact: The Wright brothers' first powered flight in 1903 lasted just 12 seconds and covered 120 feet, shorter than the wingspan of a modern Boeing 747. Sixty-six years later, the Apollo 11 lunar module Eagle landed on the Moon's Sea of Tranquility using less onboard computing power than a modern pocket calculator.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 管 originally referred to a bamboo pipe or tube, later broadening to mean 'to manage' or 'to control.'
官 (guān) gives a hint of the sound — 管 is pronounced guǎn, a connection that has shifted only slightly in tone.
王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.
贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'

example.hanzi: 网站管理员每天检查系统日志。
example.pinyin: Wǎngzhàn guǎnlǐyuán měitiān jiǎnchá xìtǒng rìzhì.
example.english: The website administrator checks the system logs every day.
example.fact: Grace Hopper, one of the first computer programmers, popularized the term 'bug' after a moth was found jammed in a relay of the Harvard Mark II computer in 1947, an incident her team literally taped into the logbook. The term stuck and is now standard across the entire software industry.

components.note: 以's oracle-bone form pictured a person bent forward holding an object, an image tied to its core meaning 'to use, by means of' — as in 以便 'so as to.'
亻 (person) — 便 relates to what makes things convenient or comfortable for a person.
更 is close in sound to an older reading of 便, though the two readings have drifted apart considerably in modern Mandarin.

example.hanzi: 他提前出发,以便赶上火车。
example.pinyin: Tā tíqián chūfā, yǐbiàn gǎnshàng huǒchē.
example.english: He left early so that he could catch the train.
example.fact: The Shinkansen bullet train, launched in Japan in 1964 ahead of the Tokyo Olympics, has carried over 10 billion passengers. In its entire operating history it has never had a passenger fatality caused by a derailment or collision.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
土 (earth) — 型 originally related to a mold made of clay used for casting
刑 (xíng) gives the sound — 型 is also pronounced xíng, an exact match

example.hanzi: 这家工厂生产小型发电机。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng shēngchǎn xiǎoxíng fādiànjī.
example.english: This factory produces small-scale generators.
example.fact: The first practical electric generator, built by Michael Faraday in 1831, was small enough to hold in two hands. It demonstrated the principle of electromagnetic induction that today powers turbines generating gigawatts of electricity worldwide.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — early tallies and charms were carved on strips of bamboo.
付 (fù) gives a sound close to fú, differing only in tone.
口 (mouth) — 号 relates to calling or crying out aloud, as well as a spoken or marked sign
丂 gives a loose sound connection to 号's reading hào

example.hanzi: 数学公式里有很多特殊符号。
example.pinyin: Shùxué gōngshì lǐ yǒu hěnduō tèshū fúhào.
example.english: There are many special symbols in mathematical formulas.
example.fact: The equals sign (=) was invented in 1557 by the Welsh mathematician Robert Recorde. He chose two parallel lines because, in his words, no two things could be more equal.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 摔 involves a hand-related action of throwing down or a body falling.
率 (shuài) gives a sound close to shuāi, sharing the same initial and a similar rhyme.
足 (foot) — 跤 describes stumbling, falling, or wrestling — all involving the feet and legs.
交 (jiāo) gives the sound — an exact match with 跤's reading.

example.hanzi: 那两个男孩在草地上摔跤。
example.pinyin: Nà liǎng gè nánhái zài cǎodì shàng shuāijiāo.
example.english: Those two boys were wrestling on the grass.
example.fact: Wrestling is depicted in cave paintings over 15,000 years old in Lascaux, France, making it one of the oldest recorded sports in human history. It was also among the original events of the ancient Olympic Games in 708 BC.

components.note: 金 (metal) reflects 鉴's original meaning "a bronze mirror," an object made of metal.
宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'

example.hanzi: 专家对这件古董进行了鉴定。
example.pinyin: Zhuānjiā duì zhè jiàn gǔdǒng jìnxíngle jiàndìng.
example.english: The expert appraised this antique.
example.fact: In 1961, art experts using X-ray and pigment analysis proved that a supposed Vermeer painting, 'Christ and the Adulteress,' was actually a 20th-century forgery. It had been painted by Han van Meegeren, who sold it to Nazi official Hermann Göring during World War II.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 仿 describes one person copying another.
方 (fāng) gives a sound close to fǎng, differing only in tone.
亻 (person) — 佛 refers to an enlightened being, the Buddha
弗 (fú) gives the sound — an exact match with 佛's reading fú

example.hanzi: 她仿佛听到了远处的雷声。
example.pinyin: Tā fǎngfú tīngdàole yuǎnchù de léishēng.
example.english: She seemed to hear thunder in the distance.
example.fact: Thunder is the sound of air rapidly expanding after being heated by a lightning bolt to temperatures hotter than the surface of the sun, around 30,000 Kelvin. Because light travels far faster than sound, counting the seconds between a flash and its thunder reveals roughly how many miles away the strike occurred.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 没 originally meant to sink or drown in water, later extended to the negative 'not have.'
殳 (shū) is the historical sound component; it no longer rhymes with méi in modern Mandarin, another case of sound drift over time.
攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.

example.hanzi: 海关没收了他携带的违禁品。
example.pinyin: Hǎiguān mòshōule tā xiédài de wéijìnpǐn.
example.english: Customs confiscated the contraband he was carrying.
example.fact: In 2019, Chinese customs officials confiscated more than 700 kilograms of elephant ivory hidden inside shipping containers labeled as timber. It was part of a global enforcement effort against wildlife trafficking that intensified after China's domestic ivory trade ban took effect in 2018.

components.note: 必's oracle-bone form pictured a stake or handle marked with a short stroke, an image later abstracted into the idea of something fixed and certain — the source of its meaning 'must, necessarily.'
雨 (rain) — something crops require to grow, giving 需 its meaning 'to need, require.'

example.hanzi: 水是人类生存必需的资源。
example.pinyin: Shuǐ shì rénlèi shēngcún bìxū de zīyuán.
example.english: Water is a resource essential to human survival.
example.fact: A human body is roughly 60% water by weight, and a person can typically survive only about three days without any water intake, compared to several weeks without food. Water is required for nearly every cellular process, including regulating body temperature.

components.note: 门 (gate/door) — 阅 originally described inspecting people or goods as they passed through a gate, later extending to 'to read, to review.'
兑 is close in sound to an older reading of 阅, a connection that has drifted apart considerably over time.
讠 (speech) — the words being spoken aloud from a text
卖 (to sell/show off) — showing off what one has learned by reading

example.hanzi: 每天阅读半小时对孩子很有好处。
example.pinyin: Měitiān yuèdú bàn xiǎoshí duì háizi hěn yǒu hǎochù.
example.english: Reading for half an hour every day is very good for children.
example.fact: The oldest known library, established by the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal around 630 BC in Nineveh, held over 30,000 clay cuneiform tablets. It has helped modern scholars reconstruct much of ancient Mesopotamian literature and science.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — the living thing in bloom.
化 (transformation) — the plant changing into blossom, the source of 花's meaning 'flower.'
艹 (plant) — the living thing in bloom.
化 (transformation) — the plant changing into blossom, the source of 花's meaning 'flower.'

example.hanzi: 他穿着一件花花绿绿的衬衫去参加派对。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhuó yī jiàn huāhuā-lǜlǜ de chènshān qù cānjiā pàiduì.
example.english: He wore a flashy, multicolored shirt to the party.
example.fact: Some of the most vividly patterned animals in nature, such as the mandarin fish and the peacock, use bright, multicolored displays for camouflage disruption or mate attraction rather than pure decoration. Biologists call this phenomenon disruptive coloration.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 伤 pairs this with a mark suggesting a cut or wound, giving the character its meaning 'injury, to wound,' as in 伤亡 'casualties.'
亡 is traditionally read as a person enclosed within a coffin or hidden away — an early image behind its meaning 'to die, to be lost.'

example.hanzi: 这次地震造成了严重的人员伤亡。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì dìzhèn zàochéngle yánzhòng de rényuán shāngwáng.
example.english: This earthquake caused serious casualties.
example.fact: The 1960 Valdivia earthquake in Chile remains the most powerful earthquake ever recorded, measuring 9.5 on the moment magnitude scale. It was strong enough to shift the Earth's axis slightly and even triggered volcanic eruptions weeks later.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — represents the act of guarding or defending.
户 (door/household) — protecting one's home gave 护 its meaning 'to protect, guard.'
王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 护士每天都要护理病人。
example.pinyin: Hùshi měitiān dōu yào hùlǐ bìngrén.
example.english: Nurses have to care for patients every day.
example.fact: Florence Nightingale, regarded as the founder of modern nursing, dramatically reduced death rates among wounded soldiers during the Crimean War in the 1850s simply by improving hygiene and sanitation in field hospitals. She documented this work using pioneering statistical charts.

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — associated with pointing toward something nearby, part of 这's role as the demonstrative 'this.'
文 is close in sound to an old reading of 这, a connection that has drifted apart considerably over time.
日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form
亻 (person) — relates to 候's meaning 'to wait, time,' as if a person watching and waiting.
矦 (hóu) gives a sound hint — 候 is pronounced hòu, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这时候,天突然下起了大雨。
example.pinyin: Zhè shíhou, tiān tūrán xiàqǐ le dàyǔ.
example.english: At this moment, it suddenly started raining heavily.
example.fact: The wettest place on Earth by average annual rainfall is Mawsynram, India, which receives roughly 11,872 millimeters, about 39 feet, of rain per year. The extreme rainfall is driven by monsoon winds funneled through the Khasi Hills.

components.note: Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'
讠 (speech) — 讲 relates to speaking, explaining, telling
井 (jǐng) gives a sound close to 讲's reading jiǎng

example.hanzi: 对我来讲,健康比金钱更重要。
example.pinyin: Duì wǒ láijiǎng, jiànkāng bǐ jīnqián gèng zhòngyào.
example.english: For me, health is more important than money.
example.fact: Studies of residents on Okinawa, Japan, one of the world's original 'Blue Zones', found unusually high rates of people living past 100. Researchers attributed this partly to a traditionally plant-heavy diet, strong community ties, and staying physically active well into old age.

components.note: 辶 (walk/movement) — 递 describes passing something along by moving it from one person to another.
弟 (dì) gives the sound — an exact match with 递.
纟 (thread/silk) — 给 originally related to supplying thread or material, later broadening to mean 'to give.'
合 (hé) gives a hint of the sound — 给 is pronounced gěi, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 她把钥匙递给了邻居。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ yàoshi dìgěile línjū.
example.english: She handed the key to her neighbor.
example.fact: The oldest known lock and key mechanism, made of wood, was discovered in the ruins of Nineveh and dates back roughly 4,000 years. Its pin-based design is essentially the same principle used in most modern pin-tumbler locks today.

components.note: 纟 (thread/silk) — 纤 describes something fine and thread-like.
千 (qiān) gives a sound close to xiān, sharing the same rhyme.
纟 (thread/silk) — 维 relates to a connecting thread or fiber, extended to mean 'to maintain, to link'
隹 (zhuī) gives a loose sound connection to 维's reading wéi

example.hanzi: 全麦面包含有丰富的纤维。
example.pinyin: Quánmài miànbāo hányǒu fēngfù de xiānwéi.
example.english: Whole wheat bread is rich in fiber.
example.fact: Spider silk, a natural protein fiber, has a tensile strength comparable to steel of the same diameter while being far more elastic. Some species' silk can stretch to nearly 40% of its length before breaking, a combination scientists have long tried to replicate synthetically.

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — 选 relates to the process of selecting, as if moving through options
先 (xiān) gives a sound close to 选's reading xuǎn
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'

example.hanzi: 委员会最终选中了这个设计方案。
example.pinyin: Wěiyuánhuì zuìzhōng xuǎnzhòngle zhège shèjì fāng'àn.
example.english: The committee finally selected this design proposal.
example.fact: The Sydney Opera House's now-iconic sail-like design, selected in a 1957 international competition, was initially considered nearly impossible to build with the construction technology of the time. Engineers spent years in trial and error before the structure could finally be completed.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 骑 describes riding on horseback.
奇 (qí) gives the sound — an exact match with 骑.
马 (simplified from 馬) depicts a horse in profile, with its mane, legs, and tail visible — later simplified into just a few strokes.

example.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢在农场骑马。
example.pinyin: Háizimen xǐhuan zài nóngchǎng qímǎ.
example.english: The kids like to ride horses on the farm.
example.fact: Horses were first domesticated by humans on the Eurasian steppes roughly 5,500 years ago. Their speed and stamina in transportation and warfare are considered one of the most transformative technological shifts in early human history, comparable in impact to the invention of the wheel.

components.note: 次 here pictures a person drooling with desire.
皿 (a dish/vessel) — coveting another's valuables gave 盗 its meaning 'to steal, to rob.'
穴 (hole) — 窃 originally described sneaking through a hole to steal.
切 (qiè) gives the sound — an exact match with 窃.

example.hanzi: 这家银行发生了一起盗窃案。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā yínháng fāshēngle yī qǐ dàoqiè'àn.
example.english: A theft occurred at this bank.
example.fact: In 1911, the Mona Lisa was stolen from the Louvre by an Italian handyman named Vincenzo Peruggia, who kept it hidden in his apartment for over two years. He was caught only after trying to sell it to an art dealer in Florence, and the theft made the painting far more famous than it had been before.

components.note: 当 is the simplified form of 當, which combined 田 (field) with 尚 as a sound element — fields of matching value being weighed against each other gave 当 its meanings 'to correspond to, to act as, ought to.'
直 (straight, upright) — 真 relates to something level and true.
几 (a small table) — an object placed level and true on a table gave 真 its meaning 'real' or 'true.'

example.hanzi: 他说的话你别当真。
example.pinyin: Tā shuō de huà nǐ bié dàngzhēn.
example.english: Don't take what he said seriously.
example.fact: In 1938, Orson Welles's radio adaptation of 'The War of the Worlds' was presented in a realistic news-bulletin format. While later accounts of mass nationwide panic were exaggerated by newspapers, some listeners who tuned in late genuinely mistook the fictional Martian invasion for a real news broadcast.

components.note: 大 (big) — 奖 describes something given as a big reward.
丬 (qiáng) gives a sound close to jiǎng.
口 (mouth), stacked three times — many mouths talking about or judging something, the source of 品's meaning 'product, item; quality, rank.'

example.hanzi: 冠军获得了一份丰厚的奖品。
example.pinyin: Guànjūn huòdéle yī fèn fēnghòu de jiǎngpǐn.
example.english: The champion received a generous prize.
example.fact: The Nobel Prize, first awarded in 1901, was funded by dynamite inventor Alfred Nobel's fortune. He reportedly restructured his will after reading a premature obituary that labeled him a 'merchant of death', choosing instead to reward achievements that benefited humanity.

components.note: 八 here depicts something splitting apart or being divided.
厶 is an old form meaning 'private' or 'one's own' — 公 shows dividing up private property to share it fairly, giving rise to the meaning 'public' or 'fair.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 这位公子出身名门望族。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi gōngzǐ chūshēn míngmén wàngzú.
example.english: This young nobleman came from a distinguished family.
example.fact: In feudal Europe, primogeniture, the practice of the eldest son inheriting the family's full estate and title, became widespread by the medieval period. It was partly meant to prevent large landholdings from being fragmented across multiple heirs, concentrating wealth and political power in a single line.

components.note: 林 here depicts eyes shut in sleep, not its usual meaning 'forest.'
夕 (evening, night) — sleeping at night is when dreams occur, giving 梦 its meaning 'dream.'
予 (to give) — 幻 is drawn as an inverted, mirror-image form of 予, picturing something turned upside down or not as it seems, giving 幻 its meaning 'illusion, fantasy.'

example.hanzi: 这座城堡看起来像梦幻中的场景。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngbǎo kànqǐlái xiàng mènghuàn zhōng de chǎngjǐng.
example.english: This castle looks like a scene from a dream.
example.fact: Neuschwanstein Castle in Bavaria, completed in the late 19th century for the reclusive King Ludwig II, was built purely as a private retreat rather than a fortress. It later became the direct visual inspiration for Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle.

components.note: 无 is the simplified form of 無, whose oracle-bone shape pictured a person dancing while holding tufts or streamers in each hand. That dance image was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the unrelated negative 'without, not have.'
疋 — a person walking, shown pausing and looking back uncertainly
矢 (an arrow/cane) — an old man's walking stick, held while hesitating

example.hanzi: 他无疑是这个领域最优秀的专家。
example.pinyin: Tā wúyí shì zhège lǐngyù zuì yōuxiù de zhuānjiā.
example.english: He is undoubtedly the best expert in this field.
example.fact: Malcolm Gladwell's popularized '10,000-hour rule' was based on research by psychologist Anders Ericsson studying violinists. Ericsson himself later clarified that the figure was an oversimplified average, since the practice needed to reach elite performance actually varies widely by field and individual.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 推 relates to pushing something with the hand
隹 (zhuī) gives a loose sound connection to 推's reading tuī
钅 (metal) — 销 originally meant to melt metal.
肖 (xiào) gives a rhyme close to xiāo, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 这个销售员擅长推销产品。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoshòuyuán shàncháng tuīxiāo chǎnpǐn.
example.english: This salesperson is skilled at marketing products.
example.fact: The door-to-door vacuum cleaner salesman became a cultural icon in the early 20th century United States. Companies like Fuller Brush and later Electrolux built entire national sales forces around direct home demonstrations, a marketing model that dominated appliance sales until television advertising took over after the 1950s.

components.note: A person's crouching body shape.
Water — represents the liquid being passed.
巾 (cloth) — held in a hand, the image behind 布's meaning 'cloth' and, by extension, 'to spread out, distribute.'

example.hanzi: 妈妈正在给宝宝换尿布。
example.pinyin: Māma zhèngzài gěi bǎobao huàn niàobù.
example.english: Mom is changing the baby's diaper.
example.fact: Disposable diapers were invented in the early 1950s by Swedish engineer and mother Marion Donovan, though major manufacturers initially rejected her design. Victor Mills, a Procter & Gamble chemist, later refined the concept into what became Pampers, launched commercially in 1961.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — held in a hand, the image behind 布's meaning 'cloth' and, by extension, 'to spread out, distribute.'
艹 (grass) — 莱 names a weedy plant, goosefoot.
来 (lái) is an exact match for the sound of 莱.
心 (heart) — 恩 relates to feelings of gratitude and kindness.
因 (yīn) gives the sound — an exact match with 恩.

example.hanzi: 我的朋友叫布莱恩,他来自加拿大。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de péngyou jiào Bùláiēn, tā láizì Jiānádà.
example.english: My friend is called Brian; he is from Canada.
example.fact: Canada has the world's longest coastline of any country, stretching approximately 202,080 kilometers, about 125,570 miles. That is longer than the coastlines of the next several countries on the list combined.

components.note: 亼 — traditionally linked to an image of gathering or covering; its original pictorial sense has become obscure, but the character came to mean 'now, the present.'
日 depicts the sun as a circle with a dot or short stroke inside — a simplified picture of the sun's disc, later squared off in the standard script.

example.hanzi: 今日新闻头条是关于气候变化的报道。
example.pinyin: Jīnrì xīnwén tóutiáo shì guānyú qìhòu biànhuà de bàodào.
example.english: Today's headline news is a report about climate change.
example.fact: The Keeling Curve, a continuous record of atmospheric carbon dioxide levels measured atop Hawaii's Mauna Loa volcano since 1958, is one of science's longest-running direct climate datasets. It shows CO2 levels rising in nearly every year measured, apart from brief pandemic-related dips.

components.note: 宣 depicts a grand hall (宀) with an open, radiating space inside, evoking a palace where proclamations were made.
折 (to break) here suggests something that must never be broken.
言 (speech) sits below — words that must not be broken, giving 誓 its meaning 'oath, vow.'

example.hanzi: 新总统在就职典礼上宣誓。
example.pinyin: Xīn zǒngtǒng zài jiùzhí diǎnlǐ shàng xuānshì.
example.english: The new president swore an oath at the inauguration ceremony.
example.fact: George Washington's 1789 presidential oath is traditionally said to have ended with the words 'so help me God,' though the phrase does not appear in the oath specified by the U.S. Constitution. Most historians consider the phrase's origin, while widely repeated by later presidents, historically unverifiable.

components.note: 女 (woman) with 覀 depicting hands on the waist — an old image of insisting or demanding something, connected to 要's meaning 'to want, to need.'
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'

example.hanzi: 快点走,要不我们会迟到的。
example.pinyin: Kuài diǎn zǒu, yàobù wǒmen huì chídào de.
example.english: Hurry up, or else we'll be late.
example.fact: Mechanical clocks with a verge-and-foliot escapement first appeared in European monasteries around the 13th century. They were built primarily to ring bells calling monks to prayer at precise canonical hours, and only became widespread for everyday timekeeping centuries later.

components.note: 心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.
An altered form of 囟 (the mind/head) — the seat of thought.
心 (heart) — thinking was pictured as an activity of both mind and heart, giving 思 its meaning 'to think.'

example.hanzi: 我猜不透她的心思。
example.pinyin: Wǒ cāi bú tòu tā de xīnsi.
example.english: I can't figure out what's on her mind.
example.fact: Studies in cognitive psychology have repeatedly shown that humans are poor at accurately judging others' emotions from facial expressions alone, with average accuracy only slightly better than chance in many controlled experiments. Popular claims about reliably reading 'micro-expressions' are far less consistent than television crime dramas suggest.

components.note: 贝 (money) — 贩 relates to trading for profit.
反 (fǎn) gives a sound close to fàn, differing only in tone.
龶 depicts a poisonous plant, tying 毒 to its meaning 'poison.'
母 (mǔ) gives a rhyme close to dú, with the initial shifted.

example.hanzi: 警方逮捕了一名贩毒嫌疑人。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng dàibǔle yī míng fàndú xiányírén.
example.english: Police arrested a drug trafficking suspect.
example.fact: The 19th-century Opium Wars between Britain and Qing-dynasty China were triggered in large part by the British East India Company's massive opium trafficking into China. The Qing government tried and failed to suppress the trade, ultimately ceding Hong Kong to Britain after its defeat.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.
另 (other, separate) — 别 relates to distinguishing one thing from another.
刂 (knife) — cutting things apart to sort them gave 别 its meaning 'to separate' or 'other,' and later, 'don't' as a command.

example.hanzi: 他们在机场依依不舍地道别。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài jīchǎng yīyī-bùshě de dàobié.
example.english: They said a reluctant goodbye at the airport.
example.fact: Heathrow Airport's Terminal 5 in London has one of the busiest arrivals halls in the world. Researchers studying it in the mid-2000s found that reunion embraces there typically lasted around three seconds on average, a small quantifiable pattern from behavioral studies of nonverbal greeting rituals.

components.note: 木 (wood) — cabinets are traditionally made of wood.
巨 (jù) gives a sound distantly related to guì, having drifted apart over time.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 衣服都放在柜子里。
example.pinyin: Yīfu dōu fàng zài guìzi lǐ.
example.english: The clothes are all kept in the cabinet.
example.fact: Traditional Chinese Ming-dynasty furniture makers, especially those working with huanghuali rosewood, often built cabinets using elaborate mortise-and-tenon joinery with no metal nails or glue at all. The joints were cut so precisely that the wood could expand and contract with humidity without the piece falling apart.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 终 originally referred to the end of a woven thread, extended to mean 'end, final'
冬 (dōng) gives a loose sound connection to 终's reading zhōng
身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.

example.hanzi: 他获得了终身教授的职位。
example.pinyin: Tā huòdéle zhōngshēn jiàoshòu de zhíwèi.
example.english: He obtained the position of tenured (lifelong) professor.
example.fact: The concept of academic tenure in the United States was formalized in the 1940 Statement of Principles on Academic Freedom and Tenure, jointly issued by the American Association of University Professors and the Association of American Colleges. It was largely a response to earlier incidents of professors being fired for expressing unpopular political views.

components.note: 乂 (a hand holding a writing tool) — the act of recording events, giving 史 its meaning 'history, chronicle.'
宓 depicts stillness and quiet beneath a roof.
山 (mountain) — a quiet, secluded mountain gave 密 its meaning 'dense, secret, close.'

斤 (axe) — 斯 originally meant 'to split, to tear apart' with an axe, a sense now mostly lost as the character came to serve as the demonstrative 'this' and, here, a phonetic syllable for transliterating foreign names.
其 is close in sound to an early reading of 斯, though the two readings have since drifted far apart.

example.hanzi: 史密斯先生是这家公司的首席执行官。
example.pinyin: Shǐmìsī xiānsheng shì zhè jiā gōngsī de shǒuxí zhíxíngguān.
example.english: Mr. Smith is the CEO of this company.
example.fact: Smith is the most common surname in both the United States and the United Kingdom, originating as an occupational name for a metalworker, someone who 'smites' or hammers metal. Related surnames like Schmidt in German and Kovač in Slavic languages carry the same meaning in their own languages.

components.note: 亻 (person) — paired with 言, the character pictures a person's spoken word as something to be trusted.
言 (speech) — a trustworthy word gave 信 its meanings 'to believe, truth,' later extending to 'letter,' as in 信封 'envelope.'
圭, made of two 土 (earth) stacked together, depicts a handful of mortar or soil.
寸 (a hand/small measure) — sealing something shut with packed mortar gave 封 its meaning 'to seal, to close.'

example.hanzi: 她把信纸装进信封里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ xìnzhǐ zhuāngjìn xìnfēng lǐ.
example.english: She put the letter paper into the envelope.
example.fact: The first adhesive postage stamp, Britain's Penny Black, was introduced in 1840 alongside a standardized flat postal rate. Mass-produced pre-gummed envelopes followed soon after, made possible by an envelope-folding machine patented in 1845 that could fold roughly 2,700 envelopes an hour.

components.note: 几 depicts a small low table or stool with legs — a simple domestic object.
千's oracle-bone form was written as the character for 'person' (人) with an added horizontal stroke to mark the numeral, a simple way of indicating a large round number, 'thousand.'

example.hanzi: 这个体育场可以容纳几千名观众。
example.pinyin: Zhège tǐyùchǎng kěyǐ róngnà jǐqiān míng guānzhòng.
example.english: This stadium can hold several thousand spectators.
example.fact: Rome's Colosseum, completed in 80 AD, could seat an estimated 50,000 to 80,000 spectators. It featured a network of underground passages and elevators, called the hypogeum, used to hoist animals and gladiators directly up into the arena floor.

components.note: 应 is the simplified form of 應, which combined a phonetic element related to 鹰 (yīng, falcon) with 心 (heart) — an inner response or feeling, the source of 应's meanings 'to respond, should.'

当 is the simplified form of 當, which combined 田 (field) with 尚 as a sound element — fields of matching value being weighed against each other gave 当 its meanings 'to correspond to, to act as, ought to.'

example.hanzi: 我们应当遵守交通规则。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yīngdāng zūnshǒu jiāotōng guīzé.
example.english: We should obey traffic rules.
example.fact: The world's first traffic light was installed in London in 1868, a gas-lit semaphore signal designed to control horse-drawn carriage traffic near the Houses of Parliament. It exploded after only a few months of use, injuring its police operator, and modern electric traffic signals did not become common until decades later in the United States.

components.note: 长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.
久's ancient form has been interpreted as a person being held back or supported from behind, an image of delay or duration that gave the character its meaning 'a long time.'

example.hanzi: 他们保持着长久的友谊。
example.pinyin: Tāmen bǎochízhe chángjiǔ de yǒuyì.
example.english: They have maintained a long-lasting friendship.
example.fact: A pair of Greenland sharks, among the longest-lived vertebrates known, are estimated by radiocarbon dating of their eye lenses to live 250 to 500 years. Some individuals swimming in the North Atlantic today may have been alive since the 16th century.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'
扌 (hand) — 拍 describes striking something lightly with the hand.
白 (bái) gives a sound distantly related to pāi, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这部电影将于下个月正式开拍。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiāng yú xià ge yuè zhèngshì kāipāi.
example.english: This film will officially begin shooting next month.
example.fact: The 1977 film 'Star Wars' had such a troubled and expensive production that 20th Century Fox executives reportedly expected it to flop before release. It went on to become, adjusted for inflation, one of the highest-grossing films in history and revived the entire science-fiction genre.

components.note: Earth — a grave is dug in the ground.
Gives the sound mò, related to mù but drifted apart over time.
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'

example.hanzi: 他们每年清明节都会去墓地扫墓。
example.pinyin: Tāmen měinián Qīngmíngjié dōuhuì qù mùdì sǎomù.
example.english: Every year at Qingming Festival, they go to the cemetery to tend the graves.
example.fact: Père Lachaise Cemetery in Paris, opened in 1804, was designed as a landscaped garden cemetery specifically to make burial more appealing after the closure of overcrowded inner-city graveyards. It now holds the remains of figures such as Chopin, Oscar Wilde, and Jim Morrison, drawing millions of visitors annually.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — something crops require to grow, giving 需 its meaning 'to need, require.'
求 originally depicted a fur coat, a meaning later kept distinct with an added 衤 in 裘. The plain form was borrowed for its sound to write the unrelated meaning 'to seek, to request.'

example.hanzi: 市场对新能源汽车的需求正在增长。
example.pinyin: Shìchǎng duì xīn néngyuán qìchē de xūqiú zhèngzài zēngzhǎng.
example.english: Market demand for new-energy vehicles is growing.
example.fact: Norway generates over 90% of its electricity from hydropower, and partly as a result, it has one of the highest rates of electric vehicle adoption in the world. By the early 2020s, battery-electric cars accounted for the large majority of new car sales in the country.

meanings: to go up by one grade

components.note: 升 originally pictured a ladle or measuring vessel used to scoop grain, giving the character its use as a unit of volume. It later extended to mean 'to rise, to ascend,' as in 升级 'to upgrade.'
纟 (thread) — 级 originally named a strand or rank of silk thread, extended to 'grade, level, rank.'
及 (jí) gives the sound — 级 is also pronounced jí, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 我把手机系统升级到了最新版本。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ shǒujī xìtǒng shēngjí dàole zuìxīn bǎnběn.
example.english: I upgraded my phone's system to the latest version.
example.fact: Moore's Law, an observation made by Intel co-founder Gordon Moore in 1965, predicted that the number of transistors on a computer chip would roughly double every two years. The semiconductor industry sustained something close to that pace for decades, though the rate of improvement has notably slowed since the 2010s.

components.note: 王 (jade, written as the radical for 玉) — 瑞 describes a jade tablet used as a token of good fortune.
耑 (duān) gives a sound distantly related to ruì, having drifted apart over time.
士's ancient form has been read as a stylized axe or tool, a badge symbolizing rank. It came to mean a man of standing — a scholar, an officer, or a soldier.

example.hanzi: 瑞士以精密的钟表制造业闻名。
example.pinyin: Ruìshì yǐ jīngmì de zhōngbiǎo zhìzào yè wénmíng.
example.english: Switzerland is famous for its precision watchmaking industry.
example.fact: Switzerland has remained officially neutral in international conflicts since 1815, following the Congress of Vienna. This long-standing neutrality is part of why Geneva became the historic headquarters of the International Red Cross and, later, several United Nations agencies.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 捣 describes pounding or striking something with the hands.
岛 (dǎo) gives the sound — an exact match with 捣.
乱 is the simplified form of 亂, which pictured tangled threads with a hand working to sort them out, an image of disorder that gave the character its meaning 'chaotic, in a mess.'

example.hanzi: 那个孩子总是在课堂上捣乱。
example.pinyin: Nàge háizi zǒngshì zài kètáng shàng dǎoluàn.
example.english: That kid is always causing trouble in class.
example.fact: Common ravens are known among corvid researchers for actively provoking other animals, including wolves and foxes, by pulling their tails or stealing food. Scientists believe this teasing behavior helps ravens test which animals might be safe to scavenge from later.

components.note: Thread — suggests something twisted or entangled.
Depicts two threads winding around each other, hence 'entangle.'
纟 (thread) — winding and wrapping are described using the thread radical.
㢆 (a rare character) gives the sound — an exact match for 缠.

example.hanzi: 这两件事纠缠在一起,很难分清。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng jiàn shì jiūchán zài yīqǐ, hěn nán fēnqīng.
example.english: These two matters are tangled together, hard to distinguish.
example.fact: In physics, quantum entanglement links two particles so that measuring one instantly correlates with the state of the other, no matter the distance between them. Einstein famously distrusted the idea, calling it 'spooky action at a distance,' though decades of experiments, including the 2022 Nobel Prize-winning work of Aspect, Clauser, and Zeilinger, have confirmed the effect is real.

components.note: 雨 (rain/storm) — the storm cloud that produces thunder
田 (fields) — the fields the storm rumbles over
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 达's meaning 'to reach, arrive, achieve.'
大 (dà) gives the sound — 达 is pronounced dá, a close match sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 机场雷达系统全天候监控飞机的位置。
example.pinyin: Jīchǎng léidá xìtǒng quán tiānhòu jiānkòng fēijī de wèizhì.
example.english: The airport's radar system monitors aircraft positions around the clock.
example.fact: Radar technology was developed independently by several nations in the 1930s, but it was Britain's Chain Home radar network, operational just before World War II, that gave the Royal Air Force crucial early warning during the Battle of Britain in 1940. This helped fighter squadrons intercept incoming German aircraft in time.
